module_summary: popstarter_path.c resolves POPStarter VCD launch paths (HDD __.POPS / PP. partitions, FAT-style mass/usb/mmce/mx4sio/ata POPS folders), builds the uLE: argument and POPSTARTER.ELF candidate list, and provides openPathForRead, the shared open helper used by POPStarter, Ember and Neutrino code. popstarter_vcd.c validates VCD headers and reads the ISO9660 PVD and SYSTEM.CNF through a generic PS1_IMAGE_READER (fd, offset, sector size). psu_functions.c writes and reads .psu save backups for the filer copy engine, including a temp-file/rename/copy-aside publish scheme. qrcodegen.c/.h are the unmodified Nayuki QR library, used only by dash_tools.c for the cloud link screen (encodeText, getSize, getModule). remote_control.c polls an FTP-dropped PS2-COMANDO.TXT inbox on ata0:. self_update.c downloads the release PSU into RAM, checks SHA-256, extracts missing sidecars through update_psu.c and overwrites the running ELF in place.

reusable_helpers.name: openPathForRead
reusable_helpers.what: opens any uLE path read-only, mounting hddN:part:pfs: paths and trying mc0/mc1 for mc:/; returns the fd and the resolved path

reusable_helpers.name: splitHddPfsPath
reusable_helpers.what: splits hddN:PARTITION:pfs:/sub into device, partition and subpath

reusable_helpers.name: prefixCaseCmp
reusable_helpers.what: ASCII case-insensitive prefix compare (0 on match)

reusable_helpers.name: readPs1SystemCnf
reusable_helpers.what: reads SYSTEM.CNF from the ISO9660 root of a raw/cooked/VCD disc image via PS1_IMAGE_READER

reusable_helpers.name: readPs1IsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor
reusable_helpers.what: finds and returns the ISO9660 primary volume descriptor of a disc image

reusable_helpers.name: readIsoLe32
reusable_helpers.what: little-endian 32-bit load from a byte pointer

reusable_helpers.name: psu_backup_copy_bytes
reusable_helpers.what: copies one file to another in 128 KB blocks and removes a partial destination on failure

reusable_helpers.name: psu_restore_name_ok
reusable_helpers.what: rejects empty, '.', '..' and separator-containing leaf names (path traversal guard)

reusable_helpers.name: parse_expected_sha
reusable_helpers.what: parses an optional 'sha256:' prefixed 64-char hex digest into 32 bytes (with hex_nibble)

reusable_helpers.name: split_parent_leaf
reusable_helpers.what: splits a device path into parent folder (with trailing / or :) and leaf name

reusable_helpers.name: overwrite_elf
reusable_helpers.what: writes a RAM buffer to a path with O_TRUNC in 16 KB chunks with progress

findings.title: File-backed PSU extractors, the extract-to-stage path and selfUpdateWriteProgress are unused by the shipped updater
findings.problem: selfUpdateInstall only calls selfUpdateLocatePsuElf and selfUpdateExtractPsuSidecarMem (self_update.c:306,327,333). selfUpdateExtractPsu, selfUpdateExtractPsuMem and selfUpdateExtractPsuSidecar have no caller in any .c/.h; only tests/test_app_packages.py:69-73 calls them. With those gone, in_open, the fd branches of read_exact/in_seek and the stage!=NULL write loop of extract_elf are unreachable, and selfUpdateWriteProgress (set at self_update.c:203) is only invoked inside that dead write loop (update_psu.c:125).
findings.fix: Delete selfUpdateExtractPsu, selfUpdateExtractPsuMem, selfUpdateExtractPsuSidecar and their prototypes, in_open and the fd field/branches of PsuIn, the stage-writing branch of extract_elf (keep locate-only), selfUpdateWriteProgress and its assignment at self_update.c:203. Point tests/test_app_packages.py at selfUpdateLocatePsuElf and selfUpdateExtractPsuSidecarMem.
findings.benefit: ~90 source lines removed (26+20+11+33 in update_psu.c, 7 header lines, fd branches). The three public functions are already dropped by --gc-sections; the static stage path and fd branches are not: a few hundred bytes of .text (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep selfUpdateExtractPsu\w*|selfUpdateWriteProgress over *.c,*.h,*.S,*.yaml: definitions in update_psu.c:183,201,335,356, prototypes self_update.h:13-18, callers only self_update.c:327,333 (SidecarMem) and 306 (LocatePsuElf). Non-C hits: tests/test_app_packages.py:69-73 (host harness) and tests/test_self_update.py:29 (asserts 'selfUpdateExtractPsu(' is absent from self_update.c). in_open used only at update_psu.c:191,344. selfUpdateWriteProgress called only at update_psu.c:125-126 inside the stage!=NULL branch; production overwrite_elf calls write_progress directly (self_update.c:238). BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:108 confirms --gc-sections.

findings.title: VCD game-ID lookup opens the VCD twice more after validateVcd through single-use readVcd* wrappers
findings.problem: popstarter.c:77 opens the VCD in validateVcd, then buildPopstarterVcdGameID opens it again in buildVcdSystemCnfGameID and a third time in buildVcdPvdTimestampGameID, each via openPathForRead (which for hdd:pfs paths calls loadHddModules and mountParty, popstarter_path.c:265-267). readPs1SystemCnf already reads the PVD, so the PVD is read twice. readVcdIsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor and readVcdSystemCnf exist only to build a PS1_IMAGE_READER for these two single callers.
findings.fix: In buildPopstarterVcdGameID open the VCD once, build one PS1_IMAGE_READER {fd, POPSTARTER_VCD_IMAGE_OFFSET, POPSTARTER_VCD_RAW_SECTOR_SIZE}, try readPs1SystemCnf + parseSystemCnfBootGameID, then readPs1IsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor + timestamp, close, then the name fallbacks. Delete the two readVcd* wrappers, their prototypes and the two static open-per-step helpers.
findings.benefit: ~30 lines removed (12 wrapper lines, 2 prototypes, the two open helpers collapse into one); one fewer open/mount and one fewer PVD sector read per VCD launch (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep readVcdIsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor / readVcdSystemCnf over src include tests: definitions popstarter_vcd.c:247,253, prototypes popstarter_internal.h:53-54, one caller each popstarter_gameid.c:115 and :205; no test mentions. buildPopstarterVcdGameID (popstarter_gameid.c:212-238) calls buildVcdSystemCnfGameID (opens at :200) then buildVcdPvdTimestampGameID (opens at :111). popstarter.c:77 validateVcd opens at popstarter_vcd.c:22. readPs1SystemCnf calls readPs1IsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor at popstarter_vcd.c:197. buildPs1ImageGameID (popstarter_gameid.c:241-259) already does the single-reader sequence for Ember images.

findings.title: neutrino_gameid.c re-implements the ISO9660 SYSTEM.CNF reader that popstarter_vcd.c already provides
findings.problem: neutrino_gameid.c has its own isoReadLe32 (=readIsoLe32), readIsoBytes (the same read-until-done loop as readPs1IsoSector:76-80), isoTextMatches (=isoNameMatches) and readIsoSystemCnf (PVD search, root directory walk, SYSTEM.CNF lookup), the same algorithm as readPs1IsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor + readPs1SystemCnf, which already accept a cooked 2048-byte ISO through PS1_IMAGE_READER {fd, 0, 2048}. neutrino_gameid.c already includes popstarter_internal.h.
findings.fix: Replace readIsoSystemCnf and its three helpers with readPs1SystemCnf on a PS1_IMAGE_READER {fd, 0, 2048}. Move the stricter checks neutrino needs (file-size bound, directory-record sanity) into readPs1SystemCnf so both callers get them, and keep parseIsoGameID.
findings.benefit: ~75 lines removed from neutrino_gameid.c (lines 20-109 minus a 3-line call), a few lines added to the shared reader; one ISO directory parser to maintain (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read neutrino_gameid.c:1-260 and popstarter_vcd.c:1-257. Both search PVD from LBA 16 for 'CD001' type 1, read root record at offset 156 (LBA +2, size +10), walk records (len, flags +25, name_len +32, name +33) for SYSTEM.CNF and read its extent. Differences: neutrino searches 32 PVD sectors vs 16, requires name_len 10/12, rejects interleaved/multi-extent records and files >= buffer; popstarter truncates to the buffer. Grep 'static u32 .*Le32' over src: neutrino_gameid.c:20, popstarter_vcd.c:3, mc_card_export.c:168. prepareNeutrinoGameID (neutrino_gameid.c:201-220) is the only caller of readIsoSystemCnf.

findings.title: qrcodegen.c is built with its 53 assert() calls live (no NDEBUG), pulling __assert_func into the ELF
findings.problem: The wLaunchELF target defines no NDEBUG (ps2.yaml:614-630), so every assert in the vendored QR library is compiled, including the ones in getModuleBounded/setModuleBounded that -O2 inlines into the module loops (qrcodegen_encodeSegmentsAdvanced is 9508 bytes). qrcodegen.o is the only object that pulls libc assert.o (__assert_func), which in turn pulls fiprintf. qrcodegen.c is the only file under src/ or ee_libs/ that uses assert.
findings.fix: Add NDEBUG to the wLaunchELF defines in ps2.yaml (no other src/ or ee_libs/ file uses assert), or put #define NDEBUG before #include <assert.h> in qrcodegen.c. Leave the library code itself unchanged.
findings.benefit: MEASURED: qrcodegen.o .text 19,492 B, libc assert.o 100 B pulled only by it. INFERRED: removing ~53 assert sites (compare/branch/4-arg call, plus expression strings), several duplicated by inlining, saves an estimated 2-5 KB.
findings.evidence: Grep 'assert\(' over src: 53 in qrcodegen.c, none elsewhere (ee_libs: 0). Grep NDEBUG ps2.yaml: none; BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:107 records wLaunchELF compile flags '-O2 -Wall -ffunction-sections'. evidence/Launchstation/raw/link/wLaunchELF-contrib-by-object.tsv:67 qrcodegen.o .text 19492 .rodata 472; link/wLaunchELF-archive-members.tsv:101 libc_a-assert.o (100 B) extracted by qrcodegen.o for __assert_func, :82 fiprintf extracted by assert.o. sizes/ds34-wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv: qrcodegen_encodeSegmentsAdvanced 9508, initializeFunctionModules 3532, drawFormatBits 1892. The byte saving was not measured.

findings.title: find_file_info allocates and lists a whole directory (2048 FILEINFO) just to read the running ELF's size
findings.problem: To learn the old ELF size for the free-space check, find_file_info memaligns sizeof(FILEINFO)*MAX_ENTRY (about 388 B x 2048 = ~776 KB) and runs getDir on the app folder, while the multi-MB update package is already held in RAM. If that allocation or the listing fails, find_file_info returns 0 and the free-space check at :341 is skipped silently.
findings.fix: Replace find_file_info with an open + genLseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END) + close on the elf path (the pattern validateVcd uses), and use that size in the check.
findings.benefit: ~18 lines removed; avoids a transient ~776 KB heap allocation and a full directory listing during the update (INFERRED: FILEINFO = 256 name + 66 title + 64 sceMcTblGetDir; MAX_ENTRY 2048).
findings.evidence: Read self_update.c:96-119 and :341-346. find_file_info has one caller (:341). FILEINFO at include/launchelf.h:560-565 (name[MAX_NAME=256], title[66], sceMcTblGetDir stats); MAX_ENTRY = 2048 at launchelf.h:205. Only stats.FileSizeByte of the match is used (:342,345). genOpen/genLseek size pattern at popstarter_vcd.c:22-26.

findings.title: psu_functions.c fills the PSU root header, the mcT_header copy and the 1 KB pad size twice each
findings.problem: The folder root header (attr, size, cTime, mTime, name, unknown_1_u16, unknown_2_u64) is built identically in psu_backup_create_root_image and psu_backup_finalize_root_image; the psu_header -> mcT_header copy is the same 7 lines in psu_restore_open_root_image and psu_restore_read_file_entry; the pad-size if/else appears twice and psu_restore_check_entries already uses the one-expression form (:402).
findings.fix: Add one static fill_root_header(psu_header*, const mcT_header*, int count) and one static copy_to_mc_header(mcT_header*, FILEINFO*, const psu_header*) used by both callers; write the pad size as (0x400 - (size & 0x3FF)) & 0x3FF in both places.
findings.justification: Each helper replaces two identical 7-8 line blocks with one, so the file shrinks.
findings.benefit: ~14 lines removed; no measurable ELF change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read psu_functions.c:1-423 and compared the cited blocks line by line: 84-92 vs 238-245 differ only in '*psu_content' vs 'psu_content'; 333-340 vs 366-372 differ only in mc_head->size (0 vs psu_head.size, set separately); 276-279 vs 361-364 identical logic.

findings.title: clear_psu_header/pad_psu_header are exported one-line memset wrappers used only inside psu_functions.c
findings.problem: Both functions only memset a psu_header; their only callers are in psu_functions.c (:84,96,238,267,289). The header exports them and tests/test_copy_psu_listing.py:276 and tests/test_listing_callers.py:239 rewrite them to static to paste the file into a host TU.
findings.fix: Delete both functions and their prototypes and use memset(&psu_head, 0 or 0xFF, sizeof psu_head) at the five call sites; drop the matching replace() calls in the two tests.
findings.benefit: ~11 lines removed (9 in .c, 2 in .h) plus 2 test lines; no ELF change, gc-sections/inlining already handle them (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep clear_psu_header|pad_psu_header over the whole repo: psu_functions.c:7,12 (defs), 84,96,238,267,289 (calls), psu_functions.h:7-8, docs/architecture-maintenance.md:104, tests/test_copy_psu_listing.py:276-277, tests/test_listing_callers.py:239-240. No other source caller.

findings.title: remoteCommandPoll stacks a second 3 s throttle under the dashboard's 500 ms one, stats before opening, and has a never-built #else stub
findings.problem: dash_main.c:1458-1461 already calls the poll every 500 ms, then remoteCommandPoll keeps its own next_remote_poll and only acts every 3000 ms, so the outer gate has no effect on it (pc_game_receiver.c:323-325 does the same). fileXioGetStat at :53 only precedes fileXioOpen, which fails the same way when the file is missing (one extra IOP RPC per poll). ETH and EXFAT are always defined (ps2.yaml:624,629), so the #else stub at :101-107 is never compiled.
findings.fix: Keep one throttle: drop next_remote_poll/REMOTE_COMMAND_INTERVAL_MS here (and next_poll in pc_game_receiver.c) and set the dash_main.c gate to the wanted interval, or the reverse. Delete the fileXioGetStat call and the #if/#else wrapper.
findings.benefit: ~15 lines removed across the two pollers; one fewer fileXio RPC per poll (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep remoteCommandPoll|next_remote_poll: only caller dash_main.c:775 (pollRemotePcCommandImpl, under #ifdef ETH) reached from :1460 inside the 500 ms gate at :1458-1461. remote_control.c:49-51 3000 ms gate. ps2.yaml:624 ETH, :629 EXFAT; configure_ds34.py only adds DS34 (brief section 2). remote_control.c:53 stat result st is never read.

findings.title: Small path-helper duplication: mc0/mc1 open blocks, elf.c copy of isHddPartyPath/isHddDevicePath, split_parent_leaf branches
findings.problem: openPathForRead repeats the open + copy-opened_path block three times (genFixPath, mc0:, mc1:) and the final opened_path copy once more; elf.c:357-365 re-defines static isHddPartyPath (identical to popstarter_path.c:124-130) and isHddBrowserPath (equal to isHddDevicePath, popstarter_path.c:20-27); split_parent_leaf has two identical branches that differ only in the separator found by strrchr.
findings.fix: In openPathForRead loop over the candidate paths with one open/copy block. Delete elf.c's two statics and use the popstarter_path.c functions via a prototype. In split_parent_leaf pick sep = strrchr('/') or else strrchr(':') and keep one copy of the branch.
findings.benefit: ~25 lines removed (about 10 in openPathForRead, 9 in elf.c, 10 in split_parent_leaf, minus a few for the loop); no ELF change worth stating (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read popstarter_path.c:278-320, elf.c:357-369, self_update.c:58-89. Grep -w isHddPartyPath: elf.c:357 (static def), 364, 748, 762; popstarter_path.c:124; popstarter.c:94; popstarter_internal.h:47. elf.c does not include popstarter_internal.h (otherwise the static would clash with the extern prototype); a one-line prototype or the include is needed.
